title: Embedded admin snippets exec API and event-driven task adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Tier-1 support often runs short procedural snippets (ad-hoc sequences of admin commands) that are brittle, hard to audit, and often lack consistent observability. We need a lightweight API that lets support engineers embed vetted admin snippets into alert-to-remediation workflows so a runbook step becomes an event-driven, auditable, and replayable task with built-in safety checks.

Goal: Build an "Exec API" + Event Adapter that: 1) Accepts a small, validated snippet (tasklet) or a reference to a stored template, 2) Executes asynchronously via an event queue with idempotency + precedence rules, 3) Emits structured telemetry for each task step, 4) Enforces RBAC/approval gates and dry-run mode, and 5) Produces a replayable audit record for postmortems and quality evals.

Scope & deliverables:
- Exec API (HTTP + SDK surface) for creating, querying, cancelling tasklets.
- Event adapter that converts runbook steps into queued tasks with retry and backoff policies tuned for infra vs product actions.
- Safety layer: preflight checks, KMS-signed templates, granular RBAC and approval-required flags.
- Telemetry: per-task metrics (enqueue->complete latency, success/failure reason, affected resources), searchable logs, and dashboard tile in Console.
- Developer tools: local dry-run harness and a simulation endpoint for safe testing.

Non-goals: building a full runbook authoring UI (Console UI tracked separately), replacing large-scale orchestration engines, or shipping adminlets that bypass security review.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts tasklet payload or template reference and returns a task id
Tasks are persisted to queue and processed by worker with idempotency token enforcement
All executed actions produce structured telemetry entries ingested into ops-telemetry with fields: task_id, step_id, action, resource, status, error_code, duration_ms
Preflight RBAC check prevents non-authorized users from executing dangerous tasklets; approval-required templates reject execution with a 403 and a link to approval flow
Dry-run mode returns a deterministic simulated result and exposes affected resources without mutating state
Security review checklist completed and signoff attached to this ticket before canary rollout

Prototype laid out idempotency via task_token; caveat: some infra actions are not idempotent at our API layer; mitigation proposed: require safe wrappers for non-idempotent actions.
